purpose: How Baltor decides whether an external repo behind a capability slot is still safe to adopt/keep. Every adapter card carries a health_status from this enum; signals drive transitions; quarantine triggers force a slot off a provider. This makes 'the upstream repo decayed' a governed, reviewable event instead of a silent liability.

monitored_signals.rationale: unpatched CVE in a dependency we route through
AGPL/SSPL/commercial relicense can make adoption illegal for our use
no future maintenance (e.g. Kuzu archived Oct 2025)
project pivoted away from the capability we need (e.g. Marqo -> ecommerce)
cannot confirm the repo is what an upstream list claims (e.g. Synapse AI)

invariants: Every adapter card has a health_status in health_status_enum.
Every slot/adapter status is in adoption_status_enum.
An active or candidate slot may NOT be wired (adapter_id) to an adapter whose health_status is decayed or archived.
A flagged/quarantined provider may never appear as a primary/fallback/stub (adopted) adapter — only in quarantined_providers, a foil card, or a reference card.
